title: Strict-local comparison reduced to a geometric strict-local fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar x$ be a geometric point of $X$, and let $\bar s=f\bar x$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $A=S_{(\bar s)}$ and $B=X_{(\bar x)}$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with their canonical map $B\to A$ [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Let $K$ be any separably closed field [def-pc-separably-closed], let $u:\operatorname{Spec}K\to A$ be any scheme morphism, let $F$ be an abelian etale sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and let $q\geq0$. Then the following two canonical pullback maps [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] are isomorphisms simultaneously: $$H^q(A\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K,F)\longrightarrow H^q(B\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K,F),$$ $$H^q(\operatorname{Spec}K,F)\longrightarrow H^q(B\times_A\operatorname{Spec}K,F).$$ Fibre products are those of [def-pc-fibre-product]; etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] on each fibre product uses the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] under its projection to $\operatorname{Spec}K$. No smoothness, properness, finite-type, torsion, or algebraicity condition on $u$ is assumed.
